candidates.phrase: the apostles confess Jesus to be the Word
candidates.rationale: Directly asserts that Jesus, the Son, is identified as the Word using John 1:1.
candidates.chunk_text: For this reason the apostles confess Jesus to be the Word: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God"; as "the image of the invisible God"; as the "radiance of the glory of God and the very stamp of his nature".

candidates.phrase: God created everything by the eternal Word, his beloved Son
candidates.rationale: Explicitly equates the eternal Word with God's beloved Son, positively identifying the Son as Logos.
candidates.chunk_text: "In the beginning was the Word. . . and the Word was God. . . all things were made through him, and without him was not anything made that was made." The New Testament reveals that God created everything by the eternal Word, his beloved Son. In him "all things were created, in heaven and on earth.. . all things were created through him and for him. He is before all things, and in him all things hold together." The Church's faith likewise confesses the creative action of the Holy Spirit, the "giver of life", "the Creator Spirit" (Veni, Creator Spiritus), the "source of every good".

candidates.phrase: Taking up St. John's expression, "The Word became flesh"
candidates.rationale: Applies John's title 'the Word' to the Son of God's Incarnation, asserting the Son's identity as the Word.
candidates.chunk_text: Taking up St. John's expression, "The Word became flesh", The Church calls "Incarnation" the fact that the Son of God assumed a human nature in order to accomplish our salvation in it. In a hymn cited by St. Paul, the Church sings the mystery of the Incarnation: Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men. and being found in human form he humbled himself and became obedient unto death, even death on a cross.

candidates.phrase: is the perfect and definitive Word of the Father
candidates.rationale: Directly identifies the only-begotten Son as the Father's Word, positively naming the Son as Logos.
candidates.chunk_text: 9. What is the full and definitive stage of God's Revelation? The full and definitive stage of God’s revelation is accomplished in his Word made flesh, Jesus Christ, the mediator and fullness of Revelation. He, being the only-begotten Son of God made man, is the perfect and definitive Word of the Father. In the sending of the Son and the gift of the Spirit, Revelation is now fully complete although the faith of the Church must gradually grasp its full significance over the course of centuries. “In giving us his Son, his only and definitive Word, God spoke everything to us at once in this sole Word, and he has no more to say.”

candidates.phrase: the Son who is his Word
candidates.rationale: States that the eternally generated Son is identical with the Father's Word, a direct kataphatic identification.
candidates.chunk_text: 46. What did Jesus Christ reveal to us about the mystery of the Father? Jesus Christ revealed to us that God is “Father”, not only insofar as he created the universe and the mankind, but above all because he eternally generated in his bosom the Son who is his Word, “ the radiance of the glory of God and the very stamp of his nature” ( Hebrews 1:3).

candidates.phrase: the one divine Person of the Word
candidates.rationale: Names the divine Person incarnate as 'the Word', linked in context to the Son of God's incarnation, a narrower but consonant identification.
candidates.chunk_text: 86. What does the word “Incarnation” mean? The Church calls the mystery of the wonderful union of the divine and human natures in the one divine Person of the Word the “Incarnation”. To bring about our salvation the Son of God was made “flesh” ( John 1:14) and became truly man. Faith in the Incarnation is a distinctive sign of the Christian faith.
